value.title: rs governance port — routes and verbs over the rs store, anomalies as a spine view, lifecycle, skills re-pointed (folds in plan 138)
value.summary: Every governance verb (project, stream, fence, dispatch/ack, canary, attest, task, node, baton/prime, anomalies, report verify, questions/decisions, close/reap, role) still executes against the frozen legacy TypeScript store while every seat lives in pij-rs; the rs store already holds the tables but exposes no route or verb. Port the governance surface to rs on one spine with stamped, broadcast descriptor events; put role on the seat row; derive anomalies from the rs spine; add close + reaper; make the legacy shim serve-or-refuse every verb with the rs name; re-point the skills and document the rs API. Plan 138's three phases are units u1/u2/u5 here.

sections.name: goals
value: One governance world: a prime, PM, coder, or UI consumer following the pij skill writes and reads only rs; `pij <governance verb>` never silently touches the legacy store.
One spine writer: every row reaches a live /v1/events subscriber with a real `at` and a decodable payload (seat.put carries the descriptor, seat.tombstone the reason).
Role is asserted by the owner (self or parent), persisted in seat_roles, joined onto /v1/seats.role and StateCard.role.

Governance records round-trip through rs: project, stream, fence, dispatch with three-state receipt, ack, canary, attest, task set, node show, baton/prime designation — over the existing tables, additive routes, v2 envelopes.
Anomalies are a derived view over the rs spine and seat rows (status-stale, unverified-done, open-question, unacked-dispatch, dead-seat), and `report verify` closes the done-is-a-claim loop.

A question asked by a seat is a durable pending decision that surfaces to its parent/prime and routes the answer back to the asker; the skill's 'ask inline, persist the pending decision' invariant has a verb behind it.
Lifecycle: `pij-rs close <id>` (owner-only tombstone) and a reaper that trusts proc{pid,proc_start}+pane, never pid alone.
Consumers can build on it: docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents the seat row, the event frame, and every governance route; chainglass renders roles and the tree with no 'not carried by pij-rs' banner.

sections.name: non_goals
value: No change to delivery semantics shipped in 134/136/137/#373/#374 (gate removal, native Copilot, omp custom-message path).

No port of watchdog, chore, focus, agent packs, bg, watch/unwatch, link/tree, compact-self, models, telegram verbs in this plan — they get an explicit refusal naming their status (ledger), not a silent legacy write.
No migration of historical legacy governance records or the 1456 unstamped seat.put rows; consumers replay from the cut.
No role inference from names, window titles, or packets — role is asserted.
No control-command (`compact`/`new`/`reload`) transport on /v1/send — sibling ledger item, separate plan.

value.text: chainglass's 4-command control (two /v1/events subscribers, one live-only, one with a since map) both receive a `report now` frame AND an `adopt` seat.put frame written while open; `grep -rn 'INSERT INTO spine_events' crates/store/src` returns only the Spine impl. Cursor never advances past an unemitted row (assert on the control).

A fresh adopt's seat.put has `at` within 1 s of wall clock and a payload decoding to the SeatDescriptor; seat.tombstone has `at` and reason. Live sqlite proof on the isolated daemon and again on production after deploy.

`pij-rs adopt %N --harness claude --role prime` ⇒ /v1/seats role=prime; `pij-rs role <id> reviewer` by the seat or its parent updates it and a third seat is refused with a decodable reason; StateCard.role follows; `pij-rs list` shows it; chainglass confirms rendering with no banner (antelope, cited).

On the isolated daemon: `pij-rs project create` → `stream create` → `fence show` → `dispatch <seat> --packet <file>` (three-state receipt: queued/delivered/acked) → recipient `ack` → `canary` → `attest` → `task set` → `node show` renders the tree with every row from the rs spine (seqs cited); the same sequence typed as legacy `pij <verb>` serves from rs (shim) with identical JSON. Also append one caller-attributed literal-kind event with spine append, observe it on both live subscribers, and show it in spine events/render without legacy writes. For every ported governance verb, native and legacy-shim --json output must be byte-identical on equivalent deterministic state, pinned as goldens.

value.claim: anomalies are a spine view; verify closes done
value.text: `pij-rs anomalies` (unscoped) lists status-stale (legacy threshold 30 min; parked seats suppressed), unverified-done, open-question, unacked-dispatch, dead-seat rows computed from rs data only; a seat that reports done and a parent that runs `report verify` clears the unverified-done row; each row carries the exact relay line as today. One named crates/core constant owns the anomaly threshold; the separate 10 min per-command stderr nudge remains unchanged. Relay detail text matches legacy byte-for-byte under deterministic inputs.

value.claim: questions are durable pending decisions with answer routing
value.text: Seat A `report question "…"` ⇒ a decision row (open) visible to A's parent via anomalies and `pij-rs decisions`; the parent `pij-rs answer <decision> "…"` ⇒ the answer is delivered to A as a pushed turn AND the row closes; unanswered rows age into status-stale for the parent. Self-answer by the asker records the resolved answerer and closes via decision.answered without a redundant push (answer_msg_id null); answers by a different authorized seat still push from that answerer. Existing /v1/send from==to refusal is unchanged. Prepared answer intent is immutable under ordinary retries. Only the current parent may explicitly supersede a terminal non-delivered intent, minting a new answer id and retaining old id/answerer/text in decision.answer-superseded. In-transit and delivered evidence refuse by name; no withdrawal/cancellation is introduced. Supersede additionally requires queue and spine to share the verified real SQL authority; mixed/fake configurations refuse E-RS-ANSWER-AUTHORITY-SPLIT naming both backends while ordinary answers remain supported.

Owner close writes seat.tombstone with at and reason and removes the row from /v1/seats; unrelated callers receive E-RS-OWNERSHIP. Auto-reap requires process confirmed dead or proc_start mismatched AND recorded pane confirmed absent; paneless seats decide on process identity alone. Unknown evidence never reaps and is reported unverifiable. Recycled-pid fixture proves no signal reaches the replacement process. Dry-run reports identical candidates without writes; run prints before/after counts. Isolated-daemon proof before handoff; production receipt pending prime deploy. Process absence requires exit1 with exactly the explicit ps header and empty stderr; exit0 with a process row is live evidence. Failed empty output, diagnostics, malformed output and signals remain UNKNOWN. Real Child kill/wait recovery stays operational. Parent repeat-close returns the existing receipt; retired self retries remain refused but name the original tombstone seq.

value.claim: legacy shim: serve or refuse, never silent legacy
value.text: For every verb in skills/pij's CLI-verb table, `pij <verb> …` either serves from rs (routed) or exits non-zero with `E-RS-UNPORTED <verb>: …` naming the ledger item; an enforcement test enumerates the table against RS_ROUTE_TABLE so a new verb cannot fall through; `pij anomalies` no longer answers from the legacy spine.

skills/pij routes (peer, node, prime, ops, 00-routing) cite rs verbs for every ported job and the refusal for every unported one (grep for legacy-only verbs = 0 in ported rows); docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents /v1/seats row fields, the StreamFrame, cursor semantics, auth, and every governance route with a request/response sample pinned as a fixture. Document terminal-only answer supersession, the in-transit withdrawal limitation, and the shared-SQL authority requirement with named mixed/fake refusal samples.

value.title: Contract + spine: one writer, stamped descriptor events (u0, u1)
value.brief: PM freezes wire contracts (assets/contracts/governance-routes.json + events). u1 makes EventBus the only spine writer; ReportService and Registry emit through it with real `at` and descriptor payloads. RED = chainglass's positive control.

value.title: Role + governance records (u2 ∥ u3)
value.brief: u2: --role on register/adopt, `pij-rs role`, seat_roles joined onto /v1/seats and StateCard, ownership self-or-parent. u3: routes + verbs over projects/streams/fences/dispatches/batons/prime_designation + canary/attest/task/node; three-state dispatch receipts.

value.title: Anomalies, verify, decisions + lifecycle (u4 ∥ u5)
value.brief: u4: anomalies derived from rs spine + rows; `report verify`; decisions (question→answer routing to the asker). u5: `close` (owner-only tombstone) + `reap` over proc{pid,proc_start}+pane with dry-run.

value.title: Re-point: shim serve-or-refuse, skills, API doc (u6)
value.brief: RS_ROUTE_TABLE covers every verb (serve or E-RS-UNPORTED); enforcement test over the skill's verb table; skills/pij routes cite rs verbs; docs/how/pij-rs-api.md + pinned fixtures; chainglass confirmation.
